headlines.title: DexCom (DXCM) Could Be 32% Undervalued Following Health Canada G7 Pregnancy Clearance
headlines.summary: DexCom (DXCM) is back in focus after Health Canada cleared its G7 sensor for use with the myLoop system powered by CamAPS FX during pregnancy, creating a tightly defined new clinical use case. headlines.title: How Pregnancy Device Approval At DexCom (DXCM) Has Changed Its Investment Story
headlines.summary: Health Canada has approved use of the Dexcom G7 continuous glucose monitoring system within the myLoop automated insulin delivery setup for pregnancy, supported by AiDAPT trial data showing improved time in pregnancy specific glucose targets without added hypoglycemia risk. This approval gives DexCom another sensor option within the myLoop ecosystem in Canada.

headlines.title: Advancing type 1 diabetes care during pregnancy: a Canadian first
headlines.summary: Health Canada has approved the use of the Dexcom G7 Continuous Glucose Monitoring System with myLoop, powered by CamAPS FX, making it the only automated insulin delivery (AID) system in Canada approved specifically for use during pregnancy.

description: DexCom, Inc., a medical device company, focuses on the design, development, and commercialization of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems for the management of diabetes and metabolic health in the United States and internationally. The company offers Dexcom G7 and G7 15 Day, an integrated continuous glucose monitoring system; Dexcom G6, a CGM system; Dexcom ONE+ to replace fingerstick blood glucose testing for diabetes treatment decisions; Stelo, a biosensor designed for adults with prediabetes and Type 2 diabetes who do not use insulin; Dexcom Share, a remote monitoring system; and Dexcom Follow application. It markets its products directly to endocrinologists, physicians, and diabetes educators. The company was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.
